about: Claims of the Answer Prompt Choice lesson: id, text, source key, locator, mark (verified / unverified / inferred / ours).

claims.text: P0, the registered prompt (configuration I2), word for word, sha256 16f22d02…: its abstain rule is 'If the passages do not contain the answer, reply with exactly NOT_IN_MATERIAL and nothing else.'

P1 word for word, sha256 e86a4fae…: passages are the only source of course facts; standard mathematics and reasoning may derive, prove or compute the answer; abstain if a fact the answer needs is not in the passages.
P2 = P1 plus 'Do not reply NOT_IN_MATERIAL only because the final result is not written in a passage; an exercise asks you to derive it.' sha256 7dd91e92….
In pilot 1 the retrieval arms abstained on 135 of 270 generations. No split of causes into prompt and retrieval was made.
The registered prompt asked for an abstention when 'the answer' was not in the passages, which is unclear for a derivation exercise. 25 of 30 pilot items are proof, derivation or numeric exercises.
Example prml:ex2.51 (prove trigonometric identities from exp(iA)): both required gold passages were in H's context, and H abstained (pilot 1, P0).
Before any dev generation under P1 or P2, the candidates, the selector and the dev item file were hashed in a pre-commit manifest (thesis-pipeline cda24f1).
Runs: the 18 gold dev items × arms R and H × 1 generation × P0, P1, P2, with the same retrieval cache and order seed; no judge call; no other candidate; no second round.
Hc was not run separately: it equals H while the router is the placeholder, so it is not counted twice.

A cell is (item, arm). Gold-present = at least one accepted gold unit in the packed list. A failure counts as an abstention. A_present and A_absent are item-weighted abstention rates; CV = share of non-abstaining cells with at least one marker and every marker naming a packed passage.

Rule: eligible iff CV ≥ 0.90; two eligible → lower A_present; a gap under 0.05 → larger D = A_absent − A_present; the winner replaces P0 only if its A_present ≤ P0's − 0.10. 0.90, 0.05 and 0.10 are operational choices, not uncertainty guarantees.
Dev runs were sealed generate-only runs: no judging, no trace; the selector prints and stores aggregates only, and no raw dev reply was opened before the selection record was committed.
Result: winner P2. A_present P0 5/12, P1 5/24, P2 1/12; A_absent P0 3/4, P1 1/12, P2 1/12; CV P0 1, P1 9/10, P2 32/33; 0 failures.
P2 beats P1 by 1/8 ≥ 0.05 and P0 by 1/3 ≥ 0.10.
P2 abstains equally with and without gold in context (D = 0), so on dev abstention no longer tracks evidence; the answered-but-unsupported risk moves to the judge and the citation proxy.
Gold presence does not establish sufficient evidence, and CV checks marker validity, not support.
Abstention is endpoint-related (an abstention scores 0 on an answerable item), so the selection is tuning on an outcome proxy, on dev only.
The winner is implemented verbatim as the core's SYSTEM prompt; G uses the same SYSTEM; I3 refuses any other text.
L answers without retrieval under its own prompt, which allows abstention, so L is not a pure closed-book condition.
Headless Claude Code has no temperature control, so answers are not deterministic; the 3 generations per item and the majority label stay.
R, H, H-collapsed and L are generated three times and the item label is the majority of three; G and the exploratory arms run once.
Order: the prompt first; then the router and k_graph on dev with the chosen prompt.
R's settings, tuned on dev by gold-evidence recall after the prompt: fusion depth 30 and 10 reranked passages (recall 89 of 216).
Configuration I4: router s7-b/2, k_graph 30, graph rank hop-balanced/1, depth 30, rerank_top 10 (config_sha256 7cae3a31…).
Pilot 1 under P0 is a historical comparator, reported beside pilot 2 and the main run; it is not an isolated prompt sensitivity, and P0 is not re-run on the main set.
Addendum C amends the registration; it does not preserve it. What is preserved: no main-pool outcome informs any choice, and every choice is fixed and hashed before the data it governs exist.
After pilot 2, no change to the prompt, router, k_graph, packing, scoring, judge prompt, sample or gate definitions in response to its outputs.
An equal cap does not mean equal tokens or equal passage counts: used tokens and list lengths differ between arms and are reported per item and arm.
In a sample of 50 (question, passage) pairs, 44 reach the cross-encoder's 512-token cap and are truncated; the effect on ranks is not measured.
Reciprocal rank fusion merges two lists, and R's list can take over the context; this dominance of one list is reported per item.
The prompt was chosen on an outcome-related quantity on dev items after pilot 1 was seen; no main-set item had been answered and no choice used the difference between H and H-collapsed.
Arm G's index is a staged build that is still running; G is not ready until it ends, and it then receives the same answer prompt and cap and answers once.
Pilot 2 runs the same 30 items with configuration I4 and all five arms; it is a development rerun with descriptive estimates.
Scope line: arms answer under a passage-restricted answering prompt; the answer model answers most items without retrieval (pilot p_L 0.93).
The hop-balanced rank keeps a backfill pass, and its hop-first output order means fusion and packing can still erase deeper-hop differences.
